result.topicName: Web APIs: requestAnimationFrame, requestIdleCallback, IntersectionObserver, MutationObserver

answers.5:
requestAnimationFrame runs right before the render pipeline. This ensures that the DOM reads and writes are faster and do not hog up the main thread. Also requestAnimationFrame has higher priority over Macrotasks thus users tend to see less Jank.

setTimeout/setInterval spin out Macro tasks these have the least priority. And are picked one at a time per event loop tick, if thats not enough for to slow the visual animations. The DOM reads and writes also hog up the main thread, while the changes done during this cycle only show up in the next renderPipeline execution.

Explain:
 (1) how this affects ordering relative to synchronous DOM mutations, Promise microtasks, and macrotasks like setTimeout 
(2) a subtle re-entrancy bug that can occur if the observer's own callback mutates the DOM node it's observing, and how to guard against it.

1. Mutation observers create a array of all the mutations and queue it at the end of microtask queue.
This works exactly like how any micro tasks work. While Other micro tasks remain queued ahead of these.
2. Since a mutation observer fires a callback to DOM change.The callback itself should not again update the DOM tree directly. One way to guard this is via linters, or effective PR reviews
